clips.send: South China Sea. China’s largest and deepest sea. About 3.5 million square kilometers — more than a third the size of the whole United States. clips.send: Bohai Sea. Almost surrounded by land. An inland sea (内海): land wraps around it on three sides — Liaoning, Hebei, Tianjin and Shandong. Very shallow: about 18 m (60 ft) deep on average — a six-storey building would stick out. About 77,000 square kilometers , a bit smaller than South Carolina. Its northern part freezes in winter. The Yellow River (Huang He) flows into it; its coast has China’s biggest offshore oilfield and the Changlu salt fields.

clips.send: Zengmu Ansha. About 4° N, in the Nansha Islands. The southernmost point of China’s territory, at about 4° N — farther south than Panama (about 9° N)! “Ansha” (暗沙) means a hidden sandbank: it lies about 20 m under the sea. From Mohe in the far north (about 53° N) to here is almost 50 degrees of latitude.
